claims.hypothesis: Is the molecular gas and dust in the inner atmosphere of IRC+10216 spherically symmetric
claims.experiment: ALMA band 6 continuum and line imaging at 27 x 19 mas of SiC2, SiS and HCN
claims.result: Continuum extensions and line emission with gaps, arcs and clumps depart from circular symmetry
claims.finding: Dust and molecule formation near the star is anisotropic

evidence.quote: The line emission arising near the star, which involves upper level energies up to some 6500 K, clearly deviates from the circular symmetry we would expect in an isotropic formation scenario.

claims.hypothesis: Do large convective cells combined with pulsation cause the anisotropic formation of dust and molecules
claims.experiment: Compare observed HCN/SiS ratio variation with angle to chemical equilibrium models of temperature sensitivity
claims.result: HCN/SiS ratio varies with position angle at fixed radius; equilibrium models show abundances change by orders of magnitude for a 10 % temperature change
claims.finding: Temperature anisotropies from convective cells interacting with the pulsation-driven wind likely drive the anisotropies

evidence.quote: It is likely that they result from anisotropies in the temperature that weight differently on the fractional abundances of HCN and SiS.
Even a moderate variation of 10% in the temperature among different regions of the stellar atmosphere can lead to orders of magnitude variations in the fractional abundances

claims.hypothesis: Can a binary companion explain the asymmetries
claims.experiment: Compare maps with companion-induced structures in the literature and with their own binary envelope models
claims.result: No spiral, disk, torus or preferred ejection direction seen; structures only 2-4 yr old; binary-only models do not make arcs and blobs
claims.finding: A companion cannot by itself explain the atmospheric-scale asymmetries, though it may reshape the outer envelope

evidence.quote: However, the structures we see at atmospheric scales are only 2 – 4 yr old, much too young for invoking the gravitational pull by any companion star or planet.
None of these models produce arcs and blobs as we do observe in the maps of the circumstellar emission.

claims.hypothesis: Are shocks responsible for the asymmetries
claims.experiment: MADEX line profiles from a pulsating envelope model compared with observed profiles through the atmosphere
claims.result: No narrow velocity features or infall signatures found
claims.finding: No evidence of shocks, although they cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: We have also found no evidence of shocks, which would have left signatures in the emission maps such as infalling material and narrow velocity features in the emission profiles
Nevertheless, we cannot rule out the existence of shocks that are not seen in our data due to effects such as excitation, gas turbulence, and opacity effects

claims.hypothesis: Do randomly launched blobs from the photosphere reproduce the observed arcs and blobs
claims.experiment: Evolving-envelope models with random density-enhanced spherical caps, with and without a companion
claims.result: Blob models produce blobs and arcs resembling the ALMA maps; control and binary-only models do not
claims.finding: Blob ejection must be included to get the anisotropic features, shaping the envelope

evidence.quote: After all this analysis we can conclude that the anisotropic features only appear if the ejection of blobs is included in the models.

why_this_data.value: Spatial resolution of previous data was insufficient to see molecular gas distribution in the atmosphere and dust formation zone

evidence.quote: Because of the lack of sufficient spatial resolution, however, the distribution of molecular gas in the stellar atmosphere and the dust formation zone of AGB carbon stars is not known, nor is how it is subsequently expelled.

why_this_method.value: Chemical equilibrium models predict enhanced abundance sensitivity to temperature at the photosphere, whereas shock chemistry models are uncertain

evidence.quote: We note that chemical equilibrium models do effectively predict an enhanced sensitivity of the chemical composition to the temperature at the photosphere

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Binary companion and atmospheric shocks as alternative explanations of the asymmetries; considered and judged insufficient (shocks not ruled out)

evidence.quote: Alternative scenarios considered to explain the asymmetries observed in IRC + 10$^{\circ}$216 are the effect of a binary companion and shocks in the atmosphere of the star.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photochemistry from a close companion's UV emission rejected because several emission voids surround the star

evidence.quote: cannot explain the asymmetries we observe at atmospheric level in the brightness distribution of SiS or HCN either, since several emission voids surround the star

limitations_admitted.value: Shocks cannot be ruled out; they may be hidden by excitation, turbulence, opacity or insufficient resolution

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, we cannot rule out the existence of shocks that are not seen in our data due to effects such as excitation, gas turbulence, and opacity effects
We note that the code aims to give qualitative information about the formation of structures in the envelope.
More accurate studies are out of the scope of the current work.

limitations_admitted.value: Mismatch of the measured position with the expected proper motion is not investigated

evidence.loc: Continuum main component fit and proper motion
evidence.quote: A deeper investigation on this issue is out of the scope of this paper

referee_caveats_inferred: The convective-cell interpretation rests on qualitative arguments; no quantitative model of HCN/SiS ratio versus angle is fitted to the data
Chemical equilibrium may not apply in a dynamic, shocked atmosphere, so abundance sensitivity to temperature is model dependent
Self-calibration, cleaning and masking choices are not given, so the clump significance and the structure of the 25 mas horseshoe cannot be checked
Central absorption and optical depth are not modelled, which can imprint asymmetric structure on the line maps
Blob models use CO J=2-1 in LTE, not the lines actually mapped (HCN, SiS, SiC2)

data_public_as_stated.value: Yes, observational products are stated as public in the ALMA, SMA and IRAM-30m archives

evidence.quote: All the observational products here used are public and available through the ALMA, SMA, and IRAM-30m archives:

code_released.value: MADEX 2012 version available as an executable; chemical equilibrium and evolving envelope models available on request only

evidence.quote: The 2012 version of the MADEX code, including spectroscopic information for approximately 3500 species, is available as an executable in:
The chemical equilibrium and the evolving envelope models are available upon request.

missing_for_reproduction: GILDAS self-calibration and imaging scripts or parameters
Line identification and channel ranges for moment or channel maps
Evolving envelope model code and blob random seeds (available on request only)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Two executions of 67 min with 43 antennas, four 1.875 GHz windows at 488 kHz channels; likely tens to a few hundred GB raw (rough guess)
reproducibility.score_reason: Data are public and central results (continuum fit) are numeric, but imaging and self-calibration use GILDAS with few parameters given, most results are qualitative morphology, and the modelling code is available only on request.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The data are public, but imaging, self-calibration and map construction details are missing, and the main conclusions are qualitative and model-based rather than numeric.
